name: Difference-in-Differences (DiD)
when_to_use: Intervention applied to one group at a point in time, with a comparable unaffected control group; compare the change (before→after) between the two groups to isolate the effect of the intervention.
notes: Compares the change in a group that received an intervention with the change in a similar group that did not, isolating the real effect. Applications: measure the impact of a policy/campaign by comparing before/after with a control group.

expected_input.question: What is the causal effect of an intervention, isolated from trends that already existed?

pdca_use: Check/Act phase: isolate the causal effect of an action implemented in a group/unit by comparing its change with an unaffected control unit — closed-form calculation (difference of means), but the parallel-trends assumption must be checked before use; cite this caveat to the user.

plain_explanation.purpose: Estimates the effect of a change by comparing who was affected with who was not, before and after.
plain_explanation.when_to_use_plain: When an intervention hit part of the cases and random assignment is not possible.
plain_explanation.data_needed: Outcome measure in two groups (affected and not), before and after.
plain_explanation.example: Measure the effect of a new policy in one region using another as reference.
plain_explanation.diagram: (after-before of affected group) - (after-before of reference group)
